problem: Zero-shot VLN-CE methods rely on costly panoramic perception, passive scene understanding, and point-level waypoint actions, making them expensive to deploy, weakly aligned with instruction semantics, and short-sighted in planning.
motivation: Humans navigate by building coherent trajectories and imagining possible futures. The authors ask whether giving zero-shot VLN agents these abilities, using only cheap egocentric RGB-D input, can beat panoramic point-level methods.
key_idea: Use a diffusion-based trajectory generator to propose candidate trajectories, imagine each one with a controllable video world model and turn it into text, and let GPT-4o pick the best, with viewpoint correction so that only egocentric RGB-D is needed.
insight: The EgoView Corrector is what makes egocentric-only input viable: on 100 episodes, SR rises from 6% (no MAE/MAC) to 35% (full), and the two parts are complementary (MAE only 16%, MAC only 12%). Imagination helps up to a limit: performance peaks at a rollout length of 18 and declines beyond it as noise accumulates (from a figure). Candidate trajectory number saturates at 4 because indoor egocentric views rarely show more than four distinct branches. Naively swapping panoramic methods to egocentric input hurts badly (Open-Nav SR drops from 19 to 7).
method: EgoView Corrector: a two-stage scheme to fix heading errors from egocentric input, using a Macro-Adjust Expert and a Micro-Adjust Controller.
Macro-Adjust Expert: GPT-4o checks whether the initial view matches the instruction and, if not, rotates 90° clockwise (up to 3 times).
Micro-Adjust Controller: CLIP-prompted FastSAM produces a walkable mask; if its area ratio is <= θ=0.1, the agent turns 30° toward the more walkable half, up to 2 times, in a consistent direction.
Trajectory Generator: the NavDP diffusion policy (DepthAnything ViT + depth ViT, transformer, conditional U-Net with DDPM) outputs 24 waypoints (dx, dy, dyaw) from RGB-D.
Trajectory Filter: farthest-first (max-min) selection on mean per-step Euclidean distance keeps CTN=4 diverse candidates.

Imagination Predictor: Dream Walker (a controllable world model, SVC) turns each trajectory into a relative camera pose sequence and renders an 18-frame rollout at 320x448; Narration Expert (Qwen-VL-Max) converts the rollout into a text narrative via five guiding questions.

Navigation Manager: the Navigator (GPT-4o) compares the narratives to the current subtask and picks a trajectory ID; the Execution Expert (GPT-4o) uses the previous view annotated with the trajectory to judge whether 0, 1, or several subtasks were completed.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen; Macro-Adjust, Navigator, Execution Expert) + Qwen-VL-Max-Latest (Narration) + pretrained NavDP diffusion policy + SVC world model + FastSAM/CLIP
setting.training_data: none (training-free; uses pretrained components, no task-specific fine-tuning)
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB-D (no panorama, no odometry)
setting.action_space: trajectory-level: 24-waypoint trajectories (x, y, yaw) selected from 4 candidates, plus in-place rotation corrections

numbers.extra: egocentric RGB-D only, no odometry; 613 trajectories in 11 unseen environments

numbers_note: The real-world results are given as success counts (Ours 12/20 overall; Office 2/5, Corridor 4/5, Classroom 3/5, Auditorium 3/5; Open-Nav 6/20; Navid 3/20). CTN and IRL ablations appear only in figures.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen, DreamNav reaches SR 32.79 and SPL 28.95 with egocentric input only, beating the strongest panoramic baseline InstructNav (SR 31.00, SPL 24.00) and the strongest egocentric baseline CA-Nav (SR 25.30, SPL 10.80, which also uses odometry). In the real world it succeeds in 12/20 trials versus 6/20 for Open-Nav and 3/20 for Navid.
limitations: Navigation error is higher than for panoramic methods (7.06 vs 6.70 for Open-Nav), since egocentric input lacks global context for re-orientation after the target is lost.
Relies on multiple large models (GPT-4o API, Qwen-VL-Max, a video world model), which adds latency and cost; long imagination rollouts accumulate noise.
Ablations use only 100 episodes, and the real-world evaluation is small (20 trials per method).
